Radios were used in the trenches during World War I. The BF Trench Set was deployed in 1915 and the Wilson Trench Set shortly thereafter, with both used for communication from Brigade to Division and Division to Corps [d1]. Later in the war, more robust wireless sets were used by observers to direct artillery fire, indicating radio use in trench-related operations [d4]. Britannica confirms that all belligerents developed and use radio as an alternate means of communication due to frequent wire cuts, with radio equipment issued to headquarters including battalions [d5].
